q22201.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates an uphill stretch of road where lorries going at low speed are likely.

explain.short: The panel shows a lorry climbing a slope: on this climb you may meet slow lorries.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'probabile presenza' means likely presence: the lorries may be there, so be ready.

q22202.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates a steep uphill stretch of road that forces lorries to slow down.

explain.short: The steep climb drawn on the panel makes heavy lorries go slowly.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'ripida salita' means steep climb: that is why the lorries slow down.

sceneParams.caption: Steep climb: lorries must slow down

q22203.en: The supplementary panel shown tells you to pay attention because slow-moving heavy vehicles are likely.

explain.short: Heavy lorries climb slowly here, so you must pay attention.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'veicoli pesanti' (heavy vehicles) means the lorries of the picture.

q22204.en: In the presence of the sign shown, the driver must moderate speed because slow-moving lorries may be present.

explain.short: Steep-hill sign plus lorry panel: slow down, a slow lorry may be ahead.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'moderare la velocità' means reduce your speed: that is what any danger sign asks.

q22205.en: The supplementary panel shown tells you to drive at a prudent speed, to avoid crashing into lorries that could be in front.

explain.short: A slow lorry may appear just ahead on the climb, so keep a careful speed.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'velocità prudenziale' means a careful speed, low enough to stop in time.

sceneParams.caption: Careful speed: a lorry may be ahead

q22206.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates a stretch of road closed because of a rear-end collision.

explain.short: The picture shows a slow lorry on a climb, not a crash; the road is open.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'tamponamento' (rear-end crash): the car behind is not hitting the lorry, it is following it.

sceneParams.caption: Not a crash: slow lorries on a climb

q22207.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates that overtaking lorries is forbidden.

explain.short: The panel only warns of slow lorries; it creates no overtaking ban.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'vietato sorpassare': a white panel cannot create a ban by itself.

sceneParams.caption: No overtaking ban: just slow lorries

q22208.en: The supplementary panel shown is found on ferry boarding piers.

explain.short: The panel stands on climbs on the road, not at ferry piers.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'pontili d'imbarco' (boarding piers): the slope in the picture is a hill, not a ramp to a ship.

sceneParams.caption: On road climbs, not at ferry piers

q22209.en: The supplementary panel shown tells you to reduce the safety distance.

explain.short: With slow lorries ahead you need MORE space, never less.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'diminuire' means reduce: the opposite of what is safe here.

sceneParams.caption: Keep a good distance from slow lorries

q22210.en: The supplementary panel shown tells you to go on with the lights on.

explain.short: The panel warns of slow lorries on a climb; it says nothing about lights.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'luci accese' (lights on): nothing in the picture is about lights.

q22211.en: The supplementary panel shown means you must sound the horn every time you overtake a lorry.

explain.short: The panel asks you to slow down, not to use the horn.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'ogni qualvolta' (every time) plus 'clacson': an invented duty.

q22212.en: The supplementary panel shown signals the possibility of being towed.

explain.short: The car follows the lorry; it is not tied to it. The panel is about slow lorries.
explain.rule: This panel warns of an uphill stretch where heavy lorries must go slowly. Moderate your speed and expect a slow lorry ahead.
explain.trap: 'trainati' (towed): the car in the picture is behind the lorry, not hooked to it.

sceneParams.caption: Not towing: slow lorries on a climb

q22213.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates that a vehicle left parked can be taken away by the tow truck.

explain.short: The tow truck on the panel means 'zona rimozione': a car parked here can be towed away.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'carro-attrezzi' (tow truck): it is the vehicle that takes your car away.

sceneParams.caption: Tow-away zone: parked cars are removed

q22214.en: The sign shown indicates that the vehicle can be moved to a municipal pound.

explain.short: No parking plus the tow-away panel: a parked car can be taken to the town's pound.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'depositeria comunale' (municipal pound) is where towed cars are kept.

sceneParams.caption: Towed cars go to the town pound

q22215.en: Where the sign shown is present, vehicles serving disabled people, with the special badge, cannot be taken to the municipal pound or blocked with wheel clamps.

explain.short: The removal and the wheel clamp do not apply to cars of disabled people that show the special badge.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'non possono' (cannot): the exception protects the badge holders.

sceneParams.caption: Disabled badge: no tow, no clamp

q22216.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates a no-parking zone with vehicle removal.

explain.short: This is the 'zona rimozione' panel: parking is banned and cars are removed.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'con rimozione' (with removal): the car is not just fined, it is taken away.

q22217.en: The sign shown provides for the removal of the vehicle or its blocking with wheel clamps.

explain.short: In a tow-away zone the car can be towed or locked with a wheel clamp.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'ganasce' are wheel clamps: a metal lock on the wheel.

q22218.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates garages equipped for roadside assistance.

explain.short: The tow truck here takes away badly parked cars; it is not a service sign.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'officine' (garages): the panel is a parking rule, not a service.

q22219.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the loading of cars onto freight trains.

explain.short: The panel shows a tow truck, and means cars parked here are removed.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'treni merce' (freight trains): there is no train in the picture.

q22220.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates a mechanic's garage equipped for oil changes.

explain.short: The tow truck panel is a parking rule: cars here get removed.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'cambio d'olio' (oil change): nothing to do with this panel.

sceneParams.caption: Tow-away zone, not an oil change

q22221.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates that roadside assistance vehicles may park.

explain.short: The panel does not allow anyone to park; it warns that cars parked here are removed.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'possono sostare' (may park): the panel is about removal, not a parking permit.

sceneParams.caption: Nobody may park: cars are removed

q22222.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates that after three hours the parked vehicle is removed or blocked.

explain.short: There is no waiting time: a car parked against the ban can be removed at once.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'dopo tre ore' (after three hours): an invented time limit.

q22223.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates a road closed because of an accident.

explain.short: The tow truck panel means tow-away zone; the road is open.
explain.rule: 'Zona rimozione' (tow-away zone): a car parked against the ban can be towed to a pound or clamped. Cars with a disabled badge are not removed or clamped.
explain.trap: 'chiusa per incidente' (closed for an accident): the tow truck is lifting a parked car, not a crashed one.

q22224.en: The supplementary panel in the figure, placed high over the carriageway together with a sign showing a place, signals the lane to take to reach that place.

explain.short: Over the road, the down arrow points to the lane that leads to the place named on the sign.
explain.rule: An arrow pointing down, over the road, ties the sign above it to the one lane under the arrow.
explain.trap: 'posto in alto' (placed high): the arrow points down at one lane.

sceneParams.caption: This lane leads to the place named

q22225.en: The supplementary panel in the figure, placed high over the carriageway together with a sign, specifies which lane the sign refers to.

explain.short: The down arrow tells you which lane the sign above it is for.
explain.rule: An arrow pointing down, over the road, ties the sign above it to the one lane under the arrow.
explain.trap: 'a quale corsia' (which lane): the arrow answers this question.

q22226.en: The supplementary panel in the figure indicates that the sign placed above it is valid only for the lane shown by the arrow.

explain.short: The sign above counts only for the lane under the arrow, not for the other lanes.
explain.rule: An arrow pointing down, over the road, ties the sign above it to the one lane under the arrow.
explain.trap: 'sola corsia' (only the lane): the other lanes are not affected.

sceneParams.caption: Valid only for the lane under the arrow

q22227.en: The supplementary panel in the figure is placed to indicate a bus stop.

explain.short: The down arrow ties a sign to one lane; it is not a bus stop sign.
explain.rule: An arrow pointing down, over the road, ties the sign above it to the one lane under the arrow.
explain.trap: 'fermata degli autobus' (bus stop): no bus in the picture.

sceneParams.caption: Lane arrow, not a bus stop

q22228.en: The supplementary panel in the figure indicates that oncoming vehicles have priority.

explain.short: The arrow only points to a lane; it says nothing about priority.
explain.rule: An arrow pointing down, over the road, ties the sign above it to the one lane under the arrow.
explain.trap: 'precedenza' (priority): that would be a narrow-road sign, not this arrow.

q22229.en: The supplementary panel in the figure indicates the end of a rule.

explain.short: The arrow says where a sign applies, not where a rule ends.
explain.rule: An arrow pointing down, over the road, ties the sign above it to the one lane under the arrow.
explain.trap: 'fine' (end): ends are shown by other signs, often with a grey bar.

q22230.en: The supplementary panel in the figure indicates the end of the MAXIMUM SPEED LIMIT sign.

explain.short: The end of a speed limit is a separate sign; this arrow only chooses a lane.
explain.rule: An arrow pointing down, over the road, ties the sign above it to the one lane under the arrow.
explain.trap: 'fine del segnale' (end of the sign): the arrow does not end anything.

sceneParams.caption: Lane arrow, not end of speed limit

q22231.en: The supplementary panel in figure (A) indicates that one or more tight bends are near.

explain.short: 'Tornante' means a hairpin bend, a very tight curve, coming up soon.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'curve strette' (tight bends): a hairpin is the tightest kind of bend.

q22232.en: The presence of one of the two supplementary panels in the figure indicates that one or more tight bends are near.

explain.short: Both panels, 'tornante' and '3 tornanti', warn of tight hairpin bends ahead.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'uno dei due' (one of the two): A and B both mean hairpins.

q22233.en: The supplementary panel in figure (B) indicates that one or more particularly dangerous bends are near.

explain.short: '3 tornanti' warns of three hairpin bends: very dangerous curves.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'particolarmente pericolose' (especially dangerous): hairpins are exactly that.

q22234.en: The presence of one of the two supplementary panels in the figure indicates that one or more particularly dangerous bends are near.

explain.short: Whether it says 'tornante' or '3 tornanti', the panel warns of dangerous hairpin bends.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'uno dei due' (one of the two): both panels have the same meaning.

q22236.en: The presence of one of the two supplementary panels in the figure can indicate one or more hairpin bends.

explain.short: Panel A means one hairpin, panel B means three: one or more hairpins.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'uno o più tornanti': A gives one, B gives the number.

q22238.en: The supplementary panel of figure B indicates the number of lanes the road has.

explain.short: The '3' counts hairpin bends, not lanes.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'numero di corsie' (number of lanes): the number goes with 'tornanti'.

q22239.en: The supplementary panel of figure B indicates how many vehicles can drive through the bend at the same time.

explain.short: The '3' tells how many hairpin bends there are, not how many vehicles fit.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'quanti veicoli' (how many vehicles): the number is about bends.

q22240.en: The supplementary panel of figure B indicates how many kilometres remain to an overpass that lets you turn back.

explain.short: The '3' is the number of hairpin bends, not kilometres.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'quanti chilometri' (how many km): there is no 'km' on the panel.

q22241.en: The supplementary panel of figure B indicates the number of motorway junctions.

explain.short: 'Tornanti' are hairpin bends on mountain roads, not motorway exits.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'svincoli autostradali' (motorway junctions): nothing to do with hairpins.

q22242.en: The presence of one of the two supplementary panels in the figure indicates a junction with a road where lorries coming from a dump join the traffic.

explain.short: Both panels warn of hairpin bends, not of a junction or lorries.
explain.rule: 'Tornante' is a hairpin bend: a very tight, dangerous curve. The number on panel B tells how many hairpins follow.
explain.trap: 'discarica' (dump): 'tornante' is a bend, not a road for lorries.

q22243.en: The supplementary panel in the figure, placed under the NO PARKING sign, indicates that parking is forbidden only at certain hours of the days shown.

explain.short: The panel limits the parking ban to Monday-Friday, 21.00 to 4.00.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'solo in determinate ore' (only at certain hours): outside them you may park.

q22244.en: The supplementary panel in the figure is placed on stretches of road where streets are cleaned with sweeper machines.

explain.short: The drawing is a street sweeper: the panel marks streets cleaned by these machines.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'autospazzatrici' (street sweepers): the vehicle in the picture.

q22245.en: The supplementary panel in the figure indicates the days and hours when the road is cleaned with sweeper machines.

explain.short: 'lun - ven 21.00 - 4.00' gives the days and hours of the cleaning.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'giorni e le ore' (days and hours): written on the panel.

q22246.en: The supplementary panel in the figure, placed under the NO PARKING sign, indicates that parking is forbidden only at some hours of the days shown.

explain.short: Parking is banned only Monday-Friday, from 21.00 to 4.00, for the cleaning.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'solo in alcune ore' (only at some hours): not all day.

sceneParams.caption: No parking only in cleaning hours

q22247.en: The supplementary panel in the figure indicates the times for putting out the rubbish.

explain.short: The times are for the street sweepers, when you may not park.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'deposito della spazzatura' (putting out rubbish): a sweeper cleans the road, it does not collect your bins.

q22248.en: The supplementary panel in the figure indicates the opening days of car washes.

explain.short: The panel shows a street sweeper and the cleaning times, not a car wash.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'autolavaggi' (car washes): sounds like cleaning, but it is the road that is cleaned.

sceneParams.caption: Street cleaning, not a car wash

q22249.en: The supplementary panel in the figure obliges you to give way to lorries.

explain.short: The panel is about parking during street cleaning, not about priority.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'precedenza' (priority): a panel cannot create a give-way duty by itself.

q22250.en: The supplementary panel in the figure, placed under the NO PARKING sign, indicates that the vehicles shown cannot park.

explain.short: The sweeper is drawn to show street cleaning; the ban is for ALL vehicles in those hours.
explain.rule: Days and hours on a panel under NO PARKING limit the ban to that time: here, while the street sweepers clean the road.
explain.trap: 'i veicoli rappresentati' (the vehicles shown): the drawing explains the reason, it does not pick the vehicles.

q22251.en: The supplementary panels in the figure are placed under right-of-way signs.

explain.short: They show the shape of the junction and go under priority signs.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'diritto di precedenza' (right of way): the thick line is the road with priority.

q22252.en: The supplementary panels in the figure indicate a junction, distinguishing the main road from the secondary roads.

explain.short: Thick line = main road, thin lines = secondary roads at the junction.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'distinguendo' (distinguishing): thick and thin lines make the difference.

sceneParams.caption: Thick = main road, thin = side roads

q22253.en: The supplementary panels in the figure, placed near a junction, indicate the course of the main road.

explain.short: The thick line shows where the main road goes: straight, or bending at the junction.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'andamento' (course, shape): the path the main road follows.

sceneParams.caption: The thick line shows the main road

q22254.en: The supplementary panels in the figure can be found under the JUNCTION WITH RIGHT OF WAY sign.

explain.short: This priority sign warns of a junction where you have priority; the panel adds its shape.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'possono trovarsi' (can be found): this is one of the signs they go with.

q22255.en: The panels in figure (B) and (C) indicate a dangerous bend.

explain.short: B and C show a junction where the main road bends; the side roads make it a junction, not a curve sign.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'curva pericolosa' (dangerous bend): the thin lines show side roads, so it is a junction.

sceneParams.caption: Junction shape, not a dangerous bend

q22256.en: The supplementary panels in the figure show how to leave the vehicle parked.

explain.short: The lines are roads at a junction, not parking positions.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'lasciare il veicolo in sosta' (leave the car parked): the panels are about priority.

q22257.en: The supplementary panels in the figure are also placed on motorways.

explain.short: Motorways have no junctions at the same level, so these panels are not used there.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'anche sulle autostrade' (also on motorways): motorways have exits, not crossroads.

q22258.en: The supplementary panels in the figure indicate dead-end roads.

explain.short: The thin lines are side roads joining the junction, not dead ends.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'senza uscita' (dead end): that is a different blue/white sign.

q22259.en: The supplementary panels in the figure indicate underpasses.

explain.short: The roads meet at the same level in a junction; no underpass is drawn.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'sottopassaggi' (underpasses): the lines cross, they do not pass under.

q22260.en: The supplementary panels in the figure indicate that the crossing roads are temporarily closed.

explain.short: The roads are open; the panel only shows which one is the main road.
explain.rule: Thick line = main road with priority; thin lines = secondary roads. The panel shows the shape of the main road at the junction.
explain.trap: 'momentaneamente interrotte' (temporarily closed): nothing is closed.

q22261.en: The sign in the figure allows access only to buses.

explain.short: No entry, 'eccetto' buses: everyone is banned except buses, so only buses may go in.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'eccetto' (except): the bus is the exception to the ban.

sceneParams.caption: No entry, except buses: you stay out

q22262.en: The sign in the figure allows only buses to pass.

explain.short: The no-entry ban applies to everyone except buses.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'eccetto' (except): it removes the ban for buses, not for others.

q22263.en: The sign in the figure indicates that all vehicles except buses may park.

explain.short: Parking sign with 'eccetto' bus: the parking area is for everyone but buses.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'tranne' = 'eccetto' (except): buses are left out of the parking.

q22264.en: The supplementary panel in the figure can be combined with an obligation sign.

explain.short: An 'eccetto' panel can exempt buses from an obligation sign too (for example a compulsory direction).
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'abbinato' (combined): the panel always works together with a sign.

sceneParams.caption: Can go under an obligation sign

q22265.en: The supplementary panel in the figure can be combined with a prohibition sign.

explain.short: Under a ban such as NO ENTRY, 'eccetto' bus lets buses through.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'divieto' (prohibition): the most common use of 'eccetto'.

sceneParams.caption: Can go under a prohibition sign

q22266.en: The sign in the figure forbids access to buses.

explain.short: It is the opposite: buses are the only vehicles allowed in.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'eccetto' (except): buses are exempt, not banned.

sceneParams.caption: Buses are the exception: they may enter

q22267.en: The sign in the figure forbids buses to pass.

explain.short: 'Eccetto' bus means the ban does not apply to buses: they may pass.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'eccetto' (except): read it as 'not for buses'.

sceneParams.caption: Buses may pass; others may not

q22268.en: The supplementary panel in the figure can stand on its own.

explain.short: A supplementary panel only changes the sign above it; alone it means nothing.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'da solo' (alone): a panel is always under a main sign.

sceneParams.caption: Never alone: always under a sign

q22269.en: The supplementary panel in the figure is valid only for city buses.

explain.short: The panel is valid for all buses, not only city ones.
explain.rule: 'Eccetto' + bus = the sign above does not apply to buses. A panel never stands alone: it only changes the sign above it.
explain.trap: 'solo' + 'urbani' (only city): the panel does not say 'urbani'.
